newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says tax reform to boost growth, investment.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says tax reform to boost growth, investment.

text.p: Germany's comprehensive tax reform could boost economic growth by a half-percentage point and investment by 1.5 percent, Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Thursday.
The bulk of the reform, which will cut corporate and income taxes to their lowest levels since the Second World War, is due to take effect in 1999.

"A 30 billion mark net tax cut in 1999, plus a 7.5 billion mark cut from the reduction of the solidarity tax already in 1998, will lead to more demand, more private investment capital, more lasting growth and more jobs," Waigel told a news conference introducing the tax reform package.
"Our tax rates will be absolutely competitive with all major industrial nations."

The reform will reduce the lowest personal income tax rate to 15 percent from the current 25.9 percent, and the top rate to 39 percent from 53 percent. For corporations, the top rate will be cut to 35 percent from 47 percent.

Waigel said part of the 82 billion marks in gross tax cuts would be made up by closing loopholes. The remainder would be raised by increasing indirect taxes such as value-added tax, although this has not yet been agreed.
